4 minutes read

Developer portals

Platform teams that already run Backstage, Grafana, Port, or Cortex can show Offing lifecycle risk next to the rest of their service catalog. Every path starts from the same offline export; only the step that publishes or pushes the catalog talks to the network. Scans themselves never leave the machine.

Portal What you get Details
Backstage Lifecycle card on each Component page integrations/backstage/
Grafana Dashboard of severity totals, deadlines, and per-service counts integrations/grafana/
Port offing-service blueprint entities with findings and next end-of-life integrations/port/
Cortex offing-lifecycle custom data on each entity integrations/cortex/

The catalog schema is offing.portal.v1. For organization-wide scanning before you wire a portal, see Organization rollout.

Export the catalog

offing export --format portal scans each path and prints one catalog for all of them. It reads bundled lifecycle data, so the step needs no network beyond fetching the package with npx. Pin the package version in CI; export --format portal first ships in a release after 0.7.1, so use that version or newer.

npx --yes @velella/offing@<version> export --format portal \
  services/api services/web services/payments \
  --report-base-url "https://ci.example.com/artifacts/offing" \
  > offing-portal.json

One path per service keeps identifiers and titles readable. --report-base-url makes each reportLink an absolute URL to the detailed Offing report your CI publishes.

GitHub Actions example that writes and uploads the file:

- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: 22
- run: npx --yes @velella/offing@<version> export --format portal services/api services/web services/payments --report-base-url "https://ci.example.com/artifacts/offing" > offing-portal.json
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: offing-portal
    path: offing-portal.json

Publish the file where the portal can read it: a mounted volume, a static bucket, a Pages site, or an internal URL. Artifact URLs that require a personal GitHub login cannot be fetched by Backstage or Grafana; put the file behind a URL or volume those systems can reach.

Backstage

The Backstage plugin reads the published export and shows finding counts, the next end-of-life date, and a report link on each Component page. It never scans a repository.

Annotate Components

Set offing.io/service-path to the scanned path that appears in the export:

metadata:
  annotations:
    offing.io/service-path: /repos/api

Install the plugin

Copy or path-link the packages from integrations/backstage/ into your Backstage workspace (they are not on npm yet):

Backend (packages/backend/src/index.ts):

backend.add(import('@offing-dev/backstage-plugin-backend'));

App config (app-config.yaml):

offing:
  portalExportSource: /var/offing/offing-portal.json
  # or an https:// URL the backend can fetch

Frontend — register the card on Component entity pages:

import { EntityOffingLifecycleCard } from '@offing-dev/backstage-plugin';

// Inside EntityLayout for kind Component:
<EntityLayout.Route path="/" title="Overview">
  <Grid container spacing={3}>
    {/* …existing cards… */}
    <Grid item md={6} xs={12}>
      <EntityOffingLifecycleCard />
    </Grid>
  </Grid>
</EntityLayout.Route>

To try the cards without a Backstage install, from this repository:

node integrations/backstage/sample-app/verify.mjs
node integrations/backstage/sample-app/serve.mjs
# open http://127.0.0.1:4173/

Grafana

Requires Grafana 10 or newer and the Infinity data source plugin. Infinity 4.x needs Grafana 11.6.11 or newer.

Install Infinity

grafana-cli plugins install yesoreyeram-infinity-datasource
# then restart Grafana

On Grafana Cloud, install Infinity from the plugin catalog. Create an Infinity data source and leave the URL empty; each panel supplies its own URL.

Import the dashboard

  1. In Grafana, go to Dashboards → New → Import and upload integrations/grafana/offing-lifecycle.json.
  2. Pick your Infinity data source for Infinity datasource.
  3. Set Portal export URL to the published offing-portal.json URL and save.

With no configuration the dashboard reads the sample catalog under integrations/grafana/sample-data/, so it renders as soon as it is imported. Point Portal export URL at your own export when you are ready. Every scan run that republishes the export updates the dashboard on its next refresh.

Port

integrations/port/map.mjs turns the export into a bulk entity upsert for the offing-service blueprint.

Create the blueprint (once)

Import integrations/port/blueprint.json in Port (Builder → Blueprints → Import) or create it with the API:

curl -sS -X POST "https://api.us.port.io/v1/blueprints" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PORT_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @integrations/port/blueprint.json

Use https://api.port.io for the Europe region.

Map and push in CI

Create a client ID and client secret in Port and store them as PORT_CLIENT_ID and PORT_CLIENT_SECRET.

- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: 22
- run: npx --yes @velella/offing@<version> export --format portal services/api services/web > offing-portal.json
- run: node integrations/port/map.mjs offing-portal.json > port-entities.json
- run: |
    TOKEN=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://api.us.port.io/v1/auth/access_token" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "{\"clientId\":\"$PORT_CLIENT_ID\",\"clientSecret\":\"$PORT_CLIENT_SECRET\"}" | jq -r .accessToken)
    curl -sS -X POST "https://api.us.port.io/v1/blueprints/offing-service/entities/bulk?upsert=true&merge=true" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      --data @port-entities.json
  env:
    PORT_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.PORT_CLIENT_ID }}
    PORT_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PORT_CLIENT_SECRET }}

upsert=true creates missing entities and updates existing ones; merge=true updates only the properties in this payload. Try the mapping locally:

node integrations/port/map.mjs integrations/port/sample-data/portal-export.json

Cortex

integrations/cortex/map.mjs turns the export into a bulk custom-data push. Each scanned path becomes one entry under its entity tag (the last path segment), with values under the key offing-lifecycle. Custom data attaches to entities that already exist; it does not create them. Make sure each service's x-cortex-tag matches the directory name you scan.

Map and push in CI

Create an API key with Edit entities and store it as CORTEX_API_TOKEN.

- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: 22
- run: npx --yes @velella/offing@<version> export --format portal services/api services/web > offing-portal.json
- run: node integrations/cortex/map.mjs offing-portal.json > cortex-custom-data.json
- run: |
    curl -sS -X PUT "https://api.getcortexapp.com/api/v1/catalog/custom-data" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $CORTEX_API_TOKEN" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      --data @cortex-custom-data.json
  env:
    CORTEX_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CORTEX_API_TOKEN }}

Use https://api.eu.cortex.io for the EU region. Try the mapping locally:

node integrations/cortex/map.mjs integrations/cortex/sample-data/portal-export.json

Privacy and network

Step Network
offing export --format portal None beyond fetching the package. Detectors read repository files and bundled data only.
Publish the JSON file Your artifact host, bucket, or Pages site
Backstage / Grafana read The backend or Infinity data source fetches the published file
Port / Cortex push CI calls the Port or Cortex API with the mapped payload

Offing does not send repository contents to an Offing service. The export carries repository-relative paths, severity counts, optional deadlines, and report links — apply the same access controls you use for scan report artifacts.
